FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A01
Deer behavior is unpredictable; an animal standing beside the road may run toward traffic when startled rather than away from it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A01
In areas known for deer, continually scan both the traveled road and its shoulders for animals. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A01
Slow when a deer crosses ahead of your vehicle or another vehicle, since deer often travel in groups and another may follow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A01
If a deer is seen beside or on the road at night, reduce speed immediately and use low beams to avoid dazzling it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A01
When an animal runs into the path, reduce speed as much as possible. The handbook warns against swerving for a deer because that can cause a collision with traffic or a departure from the roadway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A01
After a collision involving a deer, notify the police as soon as possible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A01
Be especially alert for roadside deer in early morning and late evening, while remembering that deer can also appear at other times of day. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

Misconceptions: Moving a vehicle to the safe refuge described by the rule does not alone establish fault; seeing one deer does not establish that the road is clear behind it.
Mnemonic: Stop, protect, report, exchange, then move only if safe.
Glossary: A safe refuge is a location off the traveled roadway suitable for the vehicle under the described conditions; an unattended vehicle still has an owner who must receive the required information.
Dynamic-fact isolation: Reporting thresholds, civil immunity, medical procedures, wildlife statistics and insurance practices remain dated-source review.
